The test image shows a tomato plant pulled from soil with:
- White cottony/fluffy material at the stem base near the soil line
- Stem split longitudinally showing interior
- Plant completely collapsed/dead with brown dried leaves
- Sandy soil background

This is a **stem/root** affected part. From the part index, stem candidates in our class list include: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Bacterial_Wilt, Gray_Mold, Phytophthora_Blight, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight.

The white cottony mycelium at the stem base is the hallmark of **Southern_Blight**. Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference image shows Southern_Blight's characteristic bleached/white stem lesion at the base, consistent with the test image pattern. The test image clearly shows:
- White cottony mycelium at the stem base near the soil line
- Complete plant collapse
- Girdling at the crown/soil interface

This matches Southern_Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii): "white cottony mycelium at the stem base" and "infection girdles the base of the stem at the soil line."
